proof.detail: Write L_{n-1}^{(1)}(u)=sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(-1)^k a_k with a_k=binom(n,k+1)u^k/k!. For 1<=k<=n-1, a_{k-1}/a_k=k(k+1)/((n-k)u)<=n(n-1)/u. Hence when u>=2n(n-1), every downward ratio is <=1/2, so sum_k a_k<=2a_{n-1}=2u^(n-1)/(n-1)!.
proof.step: Exact outer coefficient ratio for L_{n-1}^{(1)}

proof.detail: Using d/du L_{n-1}^{(1)}(u)=-L_{n-2}^{(2)}(u), write the latter coefficient magnitudes as c_k=binom(n,k+2)u^k/k!. Then c_{k-1}/c_k=k(k+2)/((n-k-1)u)<=n(n-2)/u<1/2 in the same outer regime. Thus |L_{n-2}^{(2)}(u)|<=2u^(n-2)/(n-2)!, and |b_n'(t)|<=3 t^-2 u^(n-1)/(n-1)! for n>=2, u=log t>=2n(n-1). The n=1 case is elementary.
The PNT estimate and outer Laguerre bound give |A(e^U)b_n(e^U)|<=2C U^(n-1)/(n-1)! exp(-d f(U)). For fixed n this also tends to zero as U->infinity, so the terminal Abel boundary vanishes.

For U>=6, f(2u)>=sqrt(2) f(u), since [f(2u)/f(u)]^5=8 log(u)/log(2u)>=2^(5/2). On dyadic blocks [2^j U,2^(j+1)U], J_n(U)=int_U^infinity u^(n-1)e^{-d f(u)}du is at most 2^(n-1)U^n sum_{j>=0}2^(jn)e^{-d f(2^jU)}. Consecutive summands have ratio at most q_n=2^n exp(-d(sqrt(2)-1)f(U)). For U=K n^2, f(U)/n -> infinity, hence q_n<=1/2 for all sufficiently large n, and J_n(U)<=2^n U^n e^{-d f(U)}.
Therefore |T_n(e^U)|<=2C U^(n-1)/(n-1)! e^{-d f(U)} + 3C 2^n U^n/(n-1)! e^{-d f(U)} for U=K n^2 and all sufficiently large n.

By Stirling, the logarithm of the dominant prefactor is at most n log n+O_K(n), whereas d f(K n^2)=Theta_{d,K}(n^(6/5)/(log n)^(1/5)). The latter dominates n log n, so the displayed bound is O_B(n^-B) for every fixed B.

statement.claim: Under the exact R5 source-order Abel identity, for every fixed K>=2 the complement T_n(X_n)=lim_{Y->infinity} sum_{X_n<m<=Y}(1-Lambda(m)) b_n(m) satisfies T_n(X_n)=O_B(n^-B) for every fixed B>0 as n->infinity. Thus the natural-order absolute-after-Abel complement route reopens at logarithmic cutoff U_n=Theta(n^2), without invoking an oscillatory/nonabsolute Laguerre theorem.
definitions: Assume the Bellotti PNT consequence |A(x)| <= C x exp(-d f(log x)) for x sufficiently large, with fixed C,d>0.
For any fixed K>=2 set U_n=K n^2 and X_n=exp(U_n), with finitely many small n enlarged if needed to enter the PNT range.
